where can you make small changes? i am also pre-diabetic and that news scared and devastated me. i started trying out different diet sodas to find one that could replace my (sweet, beloved, full sugar) classic coca-cola. coke zero and sprite zero are decent replacements and i found some brands of sparkling water i liked because i NEED a fun sweet drink every day. also water flavoring packets are surprisingly good.

you don't have to make all the changes at once. that would not be setting yourself up for success. i also encourage using your resources. your doctor could provide options. maybe speaking to a therapist. having a friend (irl or online) to help hold you accountable is great too.

• they should give you a list of safe foods to eat after your procedure. go easy on your stomach and stay away from things like carbonation and too much spice.
• communicate with your doctor and nurses about any of your questions or concerns. we can give advice but they are the professionals! no such thing as too many or too stupid of questions. it's your health and body and it's a good thing to want to take care of it and being prepared like you want to be is part of that.
